correctness.rationale: For 12<=c<=49, the embedded exact-integer verifier factors c! and checks s(c!)>c^2. For c>=50, Nagura at (c+1)/2, 2c/3, and 5c/6 supplies three disjoint primes q_i>c/2, each with v_{q_i}(c!)=1, so s(c!)>=q_1q_2q_3>=5c^3/18>c^2. For prime p>=13, if p does not divide s(c!), multiplication by p gives s(pc!)=p s(c!)>=p; if it does, then c>=p and s(pc!)=s(c!)/p>c^2/p>=p. Exact witnesses exclude 2,3,5,7,11. The finite stress test is supplementary and is not used as an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The direct source introduces the obstruction set and establishes positive density but does not classify its prime elements. Broughan gives an asymptotic for log s(n!), not the exact tail threshold. OEIS tabulates values without the theorem. Semantic published-record searches found no equivalent statement, and the closest own factorial-kernel result answers a different primality question that does not imply a quadratic lower bound.
residual_risks: An equivalent exact threshold or prime-stratum observation could exist in an obscure or unindexed source not surfaced by the searches.
The lead preprint is very recent; later versions may add observations absent from the first public version.

value.rationale: R is not an arbitrary parameter set: it is the explicit obstruction set used in the recent positive-density construction for six-factor factorial squares. Its complete prime layer is a natural infinite sub-classification, identifies the first admissible prime, and reduces an all-c condition to a sharp finite boundary via a reusable quadratic tail lemma. The result is therefore structurally tied to the motivating construction rather than a routine recomputation of sequence values.
